findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, leaving the RDS database unencrypted at rest. This exposes all stored data to anyone who gains access to the underlying storage.
publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the RDS database directly to the public internet rather than confining it to a private subnet.
backup_retention_period is set to 0, which disables automated backups, removing the ability to restore data and undermining data durability / recoverability in addition to audit trail capabilities.

The database username 'admin' is hardcoded, and the well-known default administrator account name is used, which violates guidance against carrying default administrative account names into deployed infrastructure.
The egress rule allows all traffic (protocol -1) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing a data exfiltration path and a channel to command-and-control infrastructure.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource '*' to the EC2 role, combining wildcard actions with a wildcard resource, which is equivalent to administrative access and far exceeds the least privilege required.

The RDS password is supplied as var.password and embedded in the EC2 user_data as DB_PASSWORD in plain text, making the secret readable by anyone with describe permissions on the instance and committing it into startup scripts.

The EC2 user_data embeds the database password (var.password) and endpoint in plain text within the startup script, exposing credentials to anyone with describe permission on the instance and to the AMI/instance metadata.
